description: PRD Phase 2 + Phase 3: the multi-layer AI/ML fraud detection engine implemented in pure Java (PRD Option B, taken dependency-free because scikit-learn/Tribuo/Weka cannot be downloaded), plus risk scoring, risk classification, and Explainable AI risk factors. Combines supervised-style fraud classification, unsupervised-style anomaly detection, billing-deviation analysis, duplicate detection, and provider/patient behavior analysis into a single explainable Fraud Risk Score (PRD sections 9-17, 29, 39). Runs automatically when a claim is submitted. Depends on FEAT-002.
steps: FeatureService.java (PRD section 26) in src/main/java/com/frauddetector/service/: extract a numeric feature vector from a Claim given historical context: patient age, treatment duration (discharge-admission days), total amount, component cost ratios, claims frequency for the patient, average historical claim for the patient and provider, amount deviation vs provider/procedure history, duplicate similarity score. Document each feature.

ml package src/main/java/com/frauddetector/service/ml/: (a) FraudClassifier.java - a transparent, deterministic logistic-regression-style scorer: a weighted-sum over normalized features passed through a sigmoid to yield a fraud probability in [0,1]; weights are explicit constants (documented as a stand-in for trained Random Forest/XGBoost since no training libs are available) and each contributing feature is recorded for explainability. (b) AnomalyDetector.java - an Isolation-Forest-style/statistical anomaly score: compute per-feature z-scores against the historical claim population held in repositories and combine into an anomaly score in [0,1] (claims far from the learned normal distribution score high). (c) BillingAnomalyService.java (PRD section 11) - compare the submitted amount for a (procedure[, provider]) against the historical normal range (mean/stddev or min-max) and output a billing anomaly score plus the percentage above historical average and the normal range used. (d) DuplicateDetector.java (PRD section 12) - compare the new claim against existing claims on patient, provider, date proximity, amount, diagnosis, procedure; output a duplicate probability and the id of the most similar claim. (e) ProviderRiskService.java (PRD section 13) - compute provider-level risk from average claim amount vs population average, claim count, flagged rate, duplicate rate. (f) PatientRiskService.java (PRD section 14) - frequency of claims in a window, repeated treatments, multiple hospitals for same treatment.

FraudRiskService.java (PRD section 15): combine ML fraud probability, billing anomaly, duplicate probability, provider risk, patient risk into a final risk score 0-100 using documented weights; classify via configurable thresholds (PRD section 16: 0-30 LOW, 31-60 MEDIUM, 61-80 HIGH, 81-100 CRITICAL). Thresholds live in a config object (ThresholdConfig) so they are changeable without code edits to the scorers.

Explainable AI (PRD section 17): produce an ordered list of RiskFactor(description, contribution/weight) explaining the top reasons the claim scored as it did, e.g. 'Billing amount is 74% above historical average', 'Provider has unusually high claim frequency', 'Similar claim detected within 2 days', 'Treatment duration outside normal range'. Generate these from the actual feature values and scorer outputs, not hard-coded strings.

Domain: add FraudAnalysis(analysisId,claimId,fraudProbability,billingAnomalyScore,duplicateScore,providerRiskScore,patientRiskScore,finalRiskScore,riskLevel,modelVersion,createdAt) and RiskFactor entities + FraudAnalysisRepository. Wire ClaimService.submitClaim to run FraudRiskService after persistence and store the FraudAnalysis + risk factors; include them in ClaimResponse.

Investigation (PRD sections 18-19, Phase 3): Investigation entity (investigationId,claimId,investigatorId,status,decision,notes,createdAt,updatedAt) + repository + InvestigationService + InvestigationController: GET /api/claims/{id}/analysis (returns scores + risk factors), POST /api/investigations (open), PATCH /api/investigations/{id} to record decision in {APPROVE,REJECT,ESCALATE,REQUEST_DOCUMENTS,MARK_SUSPICIOUS,FALSE_POSITIVE} and notes - restricted to INVESTIGATOR/ADMIN (demonstrates the 403 role path). GET /api/claims/high-risk returns claims with level HIGH/CRITICAL.
Config: ThresholdConfig.java holding the configurable score bands and detection thresholds; load defaults in code (optionally overridable via env vars).

Tests under src/test/java/com/frauddetector/: BillingAnomalyServiceTest (an amount far above the historical range yields HIGH billing anomaly + correct % above average using the PRD knee-surgery-style example), DuplicateDetectorTest (an identical patient+provider+date+amount claim is flagged as a duplicate; a dissimilar one is not), FraudRiskServiceTest (score composition and threshold classification: a clean baseline claim -> LOW; a claim that is inflated + duplicate + high-provider-risk -> HIGH or CRITICAL), ExplainabilityTest (risk factors are generated and reference the actual anomalies, non-empty for a flagged claim). Register in build.sh test discovery.
acceptance_criteria: Submitting a normal claim yields riskLevel LOW/MEDIUM with a low final score; submitting an inflated + duplicated claim from a high-risk provider yields HIGH or CRITICAL with a higher score.

GET /api/claims/{id}/analysis returns fraudProbability, billingAnomalyScore, duplicateScore, providerRiskScore, patientRiskScore, finalRiskScore (0-100), riskLevel, and a non-empty list of human-readable risk factors for a flagged claim.
Billing anomaly reports the percentage above historical average and the normal range, matching the computed values for a known fixture.
Risk classification respects the configurable thresholds (0-30/31-60/61-80/81-100).
PATCH /api/investigations/{id} as a CLAIM_OFFICER/PROVIDER token returns 403; as INVESTIGATOR/ADMIN it records the decision.
'./build.sh test' passes including BillingAnomalyServiceTest, DuplicateDetectorTest, FraudRiskServiceTest, ExplainabilityTest.
verification: Manual API smoke: submit a baseline claim and an inflated/duplicate claim, GET /api/claims/{id}/analysis on both and confirm the second has higher scores + populated risk factors; GET /api/claims/high-risk lists the flagged one.
findings: Implemented the full Phase 2+3 engine in pure JDK (no external deps). New code: domain FraudAnalysis/RiskFactor/Investigation; repositories FraudAnalysisRepository (findByClaimId=latest-by-createdAt, findByRiskLevels) + InvestigationRepository; config ThresholdConfig (bands 0-30/31-60/61-80/81-100, env-overridable via RISK_LOW_MAX/RISK_MEDIUM_MAX/RISK_HIGH_MAX/BILLING_ANOMALY_THRESHOLD/DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD); FeatureService (section 26 feature vector, each feature documented); ml package FraudClassifier (logreg stand-in, sigmoid of weighted normalized features, model version 'logreg-stub-v1', records per-feature contributions), AnomalyDetector (per-feature z-scores over the historical population -> [0,1]), BillingAnomalyService (section 11; mean/stddev with min/max fallback, reports anomalyScore + percentAboveAverage + normal range; billing z-score mapped z/4 so z=2 flag threshold ~0.5), DuplicateDetector (section 12; weighted similarity over patient/provider/date-proximity/amount/diagnosis/procedure, returns similarity + mostSimilarClaimId), ProviderRiskService (section 13), PatientRiskService (section 14); FraudRiskService combines the five layers with documented weights (fraud .30 incl 70/30 blend of classifier+anomaly, billing .25, duplicate .20, provider .15, patient .10) into a 0-100 score, classifies via ThresholdConfig, and builds ordered Explainable-AI RiskFactors from real feature values. Wiring: ClaimService.submitClaim runs the engine after persistence, stores FraudAnalysis, returns it inside ClaimResponse under 'fraudAnalysis'; added getAnalysis + listHighRisk. Controllers: InvestigationController adds GET /api/claims/high-risk, GET /api/claims/{id}/analysis, POST /api/investigations, PATCH /api/investigations/{id} (INVESTIGATOR/ADMIN only -> 403 otherwise). Router gained a patch() verb. IMPORTANT routing note: /api/claims/high-risk collides with /api/claims/{id} (no slash), so InvestigationController is registered BEFORE ClaimController in App.bootstrap so the literal route wins; keep that order. Tests: BillingAnomalyServiceTest (knee-surgery fixture: $87k vs $50k mean = 74% above, HIGH anomaly), DuplicateDetectorTest, FraudRiskServiceTest (clean->LOW, inflated+duplicate+high-provider-risk->HIGH/CRITICAL, thresholds configurable), ExplainabilityTest. Updated existing ClaimServiceTest for the new ClaimService constructor. build.sh auto-discovers *Test classes so no manual registration was needed. Verified: ./build.sh clean build (exit 0) and ./build.sh test (10 passed, 0 failed). Live smoke on PORT=18080 (curl must bypass the squid proxy via --noproxy/NO_PROXY and target 127.0.0.1): baseline claim MEDIUM ~38, inflated+duplicate claim CRITICAL ~80.8 with 3 populated risk factors, high-risk list includes only the flagged claim, PATCH decision returns 403 for PROVIDER and CLAIM_OFFICER and 200 (REJECT recorded) for INVESTIGATOR.
